question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹4,000 at 6.75% per annum rate of interest deposited on 22 February 2024 and withdrawn on 23 April 2024.
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total time = 7 days (Feb) + 31 days (Mar) + 23 days (Apr) = 61 days.

Since 2024 is a leap year (366 days), Time (T) = 61 ÷ 366 = 1/6 years.

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

SI = 4000 × (6.75 ÷ 100) × (1 ÷ 6) = 45

**∴ The correct answer is ₹45.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹4000

Rate of Interest (R) = 6.75% per annum

Time period: Deposited on 22 February 2024, Withdrawn on 23 April 2024

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 Principal = ₹4000 | Rate = 6.75% p.a.
 
 
•

 Simple Interest = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2024 is a leap year, so February has 29 days.

⇒ Number of days in Feb = 29 − 22 = 7 days (excluding the deposit day)

⇒ Number of days in Mar = 31 days

⇒ Number of days in Apr = 23 days (including the withdrawal day)

⇒ Total duration (T) = 7 + 31 + 23 = 61 days

⇒ Converting days to years: T = 61 ÷ 366 = 1/6 year

⇒ SI = (4000 × 6.75 × 1) ÷ (100 × 6)

⇒ SI = (40 × 6.75) ÷ 6

⇒ SI = 270 ÷ 6 = 45

**∴ The correct answer is ₹45.**

**__Additional Information__**

Day Counting Rule

When calculating interest for a specific timeline, it is an international banking standard to count either the day of deposit or the day of withdrawal, but not both.

Leap Year Conversion

A leap year has 366 days and occurs in years divisible by 4. To convert days into years during a leap year, divide the total calculated days by 366 instead of 365.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest is charged only on the original principal, whereas Compound Interest accrues on both the principal and the accumulated interest from previous periods.
